Session and standing automation grant bindings hash canonical tool arguments / domains (BindingHash) and verify Risk coverage via policy.Covers so TOCTOU argument changes or risk escalations invalidate prior grants.
Single-use consumption via hitl.Broker.Consume transitions answered prompts to executing/done under owner-instance verification, preventing replay of expired, canceled, or already-consumed approvals.

Strict JSON decoding with DisallowUnknownFields and trailing-EOF rejection enforced on tool_approval, mcp_oauth, ask_user, secure_form, and page_action response validators, plus host Scope/Access clamping against proposed AllowSession and GrantAccess.

MCP policy lookups (IsEnabled, Action, ToolRisks) fail closed on missing tenant/service/tool identity or checker errors; ResumeDecision, ResumeAnswer, and ResumeSecureForm guard against nil receivers/prompts and kind confusion.

findings.summary: validateToolApprovalResponse did not validate Scope ('once'/'session') or Access ('read'/'write'), allowed Scope/Access on rejections, and ignored trailing JSON tokens (as did validateMCPOAuthResponse, which also lacked DisallowUnknownFields and required 'authorized'); furthermore, RequestHostAndWait passed client-supplied Scope='session' when AllowSession=false and Access='write' when GrantAccess='read', allowing callers on /agent/prompts/{id} to widen a read-only host grant into a write grant.

Gate.Action failed open to DeclaredRisk(tool) (allowing readOnlyHint=true tools without approval) when tenantID==0, serviceID=='', or tool identity was empty despite a configured checker; Gate.ToolRisks likewise skipped policy lookup on missing tenant/service, ignored RiskChecker.Policy when ListByService was unimplemented, and trusted readOnlyHint instead of RiskWrite when Checker did not implement RiskChecker.

RequestSecureForm and ResolveSecureForm lacked explicit non-zero TenantID and non-blank UserID guards, SecureFormPrompt lacked nil gate/broker guards, and ResumeDecision / ResumeAnswer / ResumeSecureForm lacked nil prompt and Prompt.Kind verification before unmarshaling and consuming.

invariants_checked: Broker.Resolve enforces non-zero matching TenantID, fail-close per-user UserID matching, optional SessionID/Kind scoping (returning ErrPromptNotFound to prevent cross-session probing), and registered kind response validation before state transition.

Atomic compare-and-swap transitions in MemoryStore and SQL Store guard status, owner_instance, and lease_until so concurrent Resolve, timeout, cancellation, reaper, and Consume operations never double-consume or lose answers.
Waiter channel registration and close-once wakeup broadcast via sync/Redis pubsub are race-free under concurrent Await/Resolve/Cancel/Reap.

Orphaned pending prompts with expired owner leases are reaped prior to Resolve (suspended when suspendable, expired with owner_stopped otherwise) so answers are never recorded onto dead non-suspendable prompts.

findings.summary: Broker.Resolve checked row.TenantID != req.TenantID without rejecting zero TenantIDs, allowing an unattributed request (TenantID=0) to match an unattributed prompt row (TenantID=0) instead of failing closed with ErrTenantMismatch.

Broker.Resolve only invoked reapPending on lease-expired Pending prompts when row.Suspendable was true, allowing a non-suspendable prompt whose waiting replica had crashed to transition to a permanent zombie Answered row with no waiter or suspension state.

invariants_checked: Reviewer fails closed on nil reviewer/model, empty or mismatched SessionID, missing RequestID, empty/whitespace-only current-turn user messages, incomplete wildcard targets (TargetsComplete=false), incomplete scripts (ScriptsIncomplete=true), oversized actions (>64 KiB pre-masking), oversized current-turn transcripts (>64 KiB), model timeouts, cancellations, or tool-call attempts.

Prompt serialization isolates untrusted action fields inside structured JSON, caps earlier background messages while keeping current-turn authorization messages whole, and masks secret-named environment variables before sending prompts to external review models.

Assessment parser enforces a single JSON object (optionally inside one markdown fence without trailing text), DisallowUnknownFields, trailing-EOF rejection, and requires outcome=allow with risk_level in {low,medium} and user_authorization in {medium,high}.

findings.summary: actionOf serialized req.Env values in plaintext into the external LLM user prompt (unlike tools/host_approval.go which masks secret-looking env keys on UI cards), leaking API keys, tokens, passwords, and cookies to the review model.

Reviewer.review did not reject blank turn.SessionID or mismatched req.SessionID != turn.SessionID, accepted whitespace-only current-turn user messages, and splitTranscript dereferenced nil *types.Message entries without guarding.
parseAssessment used json.Unmarshal without DisallowUnknownFields or trailing-token EOF verification, accepting malformed multi-field / unknown-key JSON replies instead of failing closed.

invariants_checked: Decide and Offered enforce read-only mutation denial, treat unknown Risk values as destructive (Ask under auto_write/confirm, Deny under read_only), and fail closed (Deny / not offered) on any non-empty malformed AssistantAccessLevel while preserving empty default confirm semantics.

Grantable restricts in-run session grants to non-Always RiskWrite actions, Pregrantable restricts standing automation grants to non-Always RiskWrite/RiskDestructive actions, and Covers requires both granted and call Risk values to be valid with call risk not exceeding granted risk.

findings.summary: Offered checked level != AssistantAccessReadOnly without validating non-empty levels via level.Valid(), causing malformed access levels (e.g. 'readonly', 'none', 'bogus') to fail open (offering mutating/destructive tools and returning Allow on read/probe); Covers also did not explicitly require granted.Valid().

invariants_checked: Extension origin validation (validExtensionOrigin) strictly requires chrome-extension://<32 lowercase a-p chars> on both AuthorizeHTTP and WebSocket ServeHTTP, blocking arbitrary web page CSRF and DNS-rebinding hijacks.

Pairing and renewal token handling stores only SHA-256 hex digests in DB, enforces single-use atomic pairing exchange, requires explicit 'Bearer ' authorization header scheme, validates canonical 32-byte base64url tokens on both HTTP and WebSocket subprotocol entry points, and uses subtle.ConstantTimeCompare for secret/token equality checks.

Daemon Unix socket gatekeeper enforces 0700 private runtime directories (rejecting /tmp, /var/tmp, /private/tmp), constant-time per-daemon secret verification before proxying to inner bsk socket, and 24 MiB frame bounds.
Cluster inter-node RPC verifies HMAC-SHA256 signatures with hmac.Equal over timestamp + method + path + body, enforces 60s clock skew and nonce replay cache, and restricts internal forwarding URLs.
Multi-tenant and per-user Scope{Tenant, User} isolation binds device records, leases, and conversation task maps, stripping caller-supplied session_id / browser_instance_id overrides.

Navigation URL validation (navigate and tab_create) rejects dangerous schemes (file://, javascript:, chrome:, chrome-extension:, data:, devtools:, view-source:), control characters, and missing hosts before auto-starting sessions or dispatching RPCs.

WebSocket/HTTP body and screenshot preview payload bounds (ReadLimit, http.MaxBytesReader, maxFrame, preview size checks) and concurrent disconnect/pause/cancel races verified under -race; reserved BrowserSkill identifiers preserved per REBRAND_RESERVED.md with zero weknora/wk_ residues.

AuthorizeHTTP used strings.TrimPrefix(..., 'Bearer '), accepting raw tokens without a 'Bearer ' prefix and comparing token == input.NextToken non-constant-time; ServeHTTP checked len(token) != 43 instead of canonical 32-byte base64url validToken(token) before querying storage.

invariants_checked: Service.Run enforces shipped ApprovalMode only (ModeAuto, ModeAsk), resolves WorkDir through PathGuard.CheckDir (O_NOFOLLOW directory walk), serialises concurrent operations per workspace root via ref-counted rootLocks while running approval prompts outside the root lock, and masks secret assignments in command preview logs.

FileApproval binds out-of-scope file writes to both the SHA-256 content digest and the originating SessionID, and readForChange rejects non-regular files via Lstat before reading.
Session state (grants, delete rules, approval mode overrides) is keyed per sessionID, mutex-protected under -race, and released cleanly on ReleaseSession; zero weknora/wk_ residues.

FileApproval lacked SessionID binding and readForChange did not reject non-regular files (symlinks, FIFOs, devices) via Lstat before opening target paths during AuthorizeFileChange.

Adapter.StatSessionFile, Adapter.ListSessionFiles, and InstallManager.StatSessionFile classified symlinks and special files as RemoteEntryFile instead of RemoteEntryOther, and ListSessionFiles ignored ctx.Err() during WalkDir traversal.

invariants_checked: PolicyBuilder and Escalation protect credential roots (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.gnupg, ~/.kube, ~/Library/Keychains, appData, .bsk), shell startup files, system/root directories, home dot-directories, and .git metadata (including worktrees and bare repos with HEAD+objects+refs), resolving symlinks on longest existing prefixes before granting access.

BuildCommandEnv and FilterInheritedEnv allowlist safe locale/toolchain host variables, strip dynamic-linker injection (LD_*, DYLD_*), runtime startup hooks (NODE_OPTIONS, PYTHONSTARTUP, RUBYOPT, PERL5OPT, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, BASH_ENV, ENV, PROMPT_COMMAND, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, etc.) case-insensitively, reject '=' and NUL smuggling in keys/values, and force GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0.

Command delete classification covers rm/rmdir/unlink, find (-delete/-exec rm, BSD/GNU pre-path flags, symlink-following -L/-H/-follow), git (clean/rm with -C, -C<dir>, --work-tree, --git-dir, and escaping pathspecs), shell -c, eval, substitutions, and env/sudo wrappers (-C/-D/--chdir, env -S/--split-string); zero weknora/wk_ residues.

findings.summary: ClassifyCommand, DeleteLocations, and DeletesStayBelow missed attached/long git directory options (-C<dir>, --work-tree, --git-dir), git rm/clean pathspecs escaping cwd, BSD/GNU find pre-path flags (-L, -H, -P, -f <path>) and symlink-following (-L, -H, -follow), and wrapper chdir/split-string forms (env -C, sudo -D, env -S, --split-string), allowing destructive out-of-cwd or root/home deletes to bypass dangerous-command refusal or ModeAuto review.

PathGuard.allowWrite (used by WriteFile and MkdirAll) omitted g.writeDenied(path) (Policy.DenyWrite), NewPathGuard did not resolve symlink aliases on DenyRead, DenyWrite, and ReadOnlySubpaths, and Policy/PathGuard accepted NUL bytes in path strings.

PathGuard.ReadFile and WriteFile opened leaf files without O_NONBLOCK and without verifying S_IFREG (allowing workspace FIFOs to block goroutines forever in openat while holding workspace locks, or writes to non-regular files), and ReadFile used unbounded io.ReadAll.

BuildCommandEnv matched blockedExplicitEnv case-sensitively, allowed '=' and NUL bytes in explicit env keys/values (enabling KEY=VAL smuggling past exact-name blocklist lookup when flattened by EnvSlice), and did not normalize mixed-case Windows Path.

invariants_checked: Seatbelt compiler never interpolates paths directly into SBPL source: every dynamic path is passed out-of-band via sandbox-exec -D KEY=VALUE parameters and referenced through (param "..."), eliminating quote/parenthesis/newline SBPL injection.

resolvePolicyPaths canonicalizes WritableRoots, ReadOnlySubpaths, WritableFiles, ReadableRoots, PrivateRoots, DenyRead, DenyWrite, and Cwd via EvalSymlinks on longest existing prefixes so macOS /var -> /private/var and /tmp -> /private/tmp symlinks match kernel path evaluation.

Base SBPL profile denies default operations, restricts network unless NetworkUnrestricted, confines file-write* to parameterized writable roots/files, carves out PrivateRoots/DenyRead, DenyWrite, ReadOnlySubpaths, and .git metadata (last-rule-wins), hardcodes /usr/bin/sandbox-exec, spawns with Setpgid: true, and redirects TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP to Cwd.

findings.summary: seatbeltProcess.Kill unlocked p.mu prior to syscall.Kill(-pid, SIGKILL) (leaving a race window with Wait reaping pid) and lacked a post-kill pipe close fallback for escaped setsid() descendants, and withSandboxTemp stripped inherited TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP case-sensitively.

Advisory locks open <root>/.locks/<name>.lock with O_NOFOLLOW on Unix and enforce process-local mutual exclusion on non-Unix platforms, with idempotent sync.Once unlock functions; zero weknora/wk_ residues.

Outbound service URLs, OAuth metadata URLs, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, registration_endpoint, and authorization redirects are validated against SSRF/private IP rules and same-origin redirect restrictions.

MCP SSE and Streamable HTTP transports pin all requests (including server-pushed SSE endpoint events and mid-stream updates) to the configured service origin (scheme + canonical host:port) without embedded userinfo or fragments, preventing credential leakage on scheme downgrades or poisoned endpoints.
OAuth runtime refreshes on MCP clients validate discovered authorization-server metadata before posting refresh tokens.

MCPManager isolates cached OAuth connections per (serviceID, tenantID, principal) and isolates builtin non-OAuth connections per tenant, while rejecting cross-tenant access to non-builtin tenant-owned services.

MCPManager keyed cached OAuth clients solely by serviceID + principal.StorageID() without tenantID (causing cross-tenant OAuth client/token-store reuse on shared builtin services when a web user switched workspaces) and did not reject cross-tenant callers on non-builtin tenant-owned services.

invariants_checked: Every MCP tool call is gated by endpointFromContext, ep.HasTool allowlist, per-endpoint rate limiting, and tenant/KB/document scope resolution strictly derived from the authenticated MCPEndpoint context (never caller-supplied tenant IDs).

Cross-tenant knowledge bases, documents, agents, and wiki pages are rejected unless explicitly shared via organization KB shares, with owner-tenant execution context and Caller/TenantAPIKeyScope preserved.
All mutating document tools (add_document, update_document, delete_document) enforce access.RequireKBWrite(ctx, kb) before invoking KnowledgeService.

Inbound Streamable HTTP POST request bodies are capped at 4 MiB (returning HTTP 413 without unbounded io.ReadAll buffering), grep regexes and pagination limits are bounded, and spawned QA/touchLastUsed goroutines isolate panics cleanly under -race.

handleAsk propagates stream/agent execution errors as IsError: true even after partial text chunks were emitted, preventing truncated partial output from being returned as a successful answer or minting public resource URLs.

findings.summary: Published /mcp/:endpoint_id Streamable HTTP handler delegated directly to mcp-go StreamableHTTPServer (which runs io.ReadAll(r.Body) with no size limit), allowing oversized POST bodies to exhaust server memory.

handleUpdateDocument and handleDeleteDocument omitted access.RequireKBWrite(ctx, kb) at the MCP handler admission boundary (unlike handleAddDocument), failing to enforce APIKeyCapabilityIngest before calling KnowledgeService.

Spawned goroutines in runQA (KnowledgeQA/AgentQA) and touchLastUsed lacked panic recovery (server.WithRecovery only wraps synchronous handler goroutines), allowing downstream panics to crash the entire server process.

invariants_checked: Container security defaults: Docker container creation drops all capabilities (CapDrop=ALL), sets no-new-privileges, enforces PID/memory/CPU limits, avoids host network/privileged mode, and validates host bind-mount paths and symlink targets.

Command & shell script injection safety: dockerExecCommand passes user commands via positional arguments ($1 / $@), ShellQuote escapes shell metacharacters, and ShellJobSubmitScriptWithBackend/shellJobWrapperScript/ShellJobCancelScript validate ValidShellJobID (^sj_[0-9a-f]{4}$) and single-quote paths.

Secret & credential isolation: Cube data-plane INFO logging logs only command lines prior to wrapWithStdin heredoc wrapping and logs credential presence rather than raw tokens; secret_fill encrypts AES-GCM envelopes and cleans temporary material; gatewaySplitTransport sends inbound traffic tokens only to verified gateway targets with SSRF guards.

Cross-tenant & shared-machine session isolation: SessionBoundManager enforces tenant/session/config ownership on bindings, strips client-supplied AttachPID on shared user machines, validates terminal/shell working directories via workspace.CleanWorkDirIn, and protects read-only attachment input trees.

Concurrency, lock ordering, & memory bounds: lifecycle/turn/rewind Redis locks use token-verified compare-and-delete/renew Lua scripts; DockerRemoteClient.streamExec and ReadFile bound buffered stdout/stderr streams to 64 MiB and reject oversize ReadFile streams without host OOM or silent truncation; Redis traffic token patching uses escape-aware JSON key scanning.

GENYEE rebrand & contract alignment: verified com.genyee.sandbox.* labels, GENYEE_* env vars, /var/lib/genyee & /opt/genyee/tenant/skills paths, genyee/genyee-desktop template names, and zero weknora/knora/wk_ residues across all 136 files.

findings.summary: ShellJobSubmitScriptWithBackend, shellJobWrapperScript, and ShellJobCancelScript interpolated job.ID / meta.ID into /bin/sh scripts (using Go %q double-quoting or unquoted path segments) without checking ValidShellJobID, allowing shell command/path injection if a malformed job ID reached script builders.

CubeRemoteClient.Exec wrapped request.Stdin into the shell heredoc command before calling logCubeDataPlaneExec, leaking full plaintext Stdin payloads (including secret material and file contents) into INFO logs.

DockerRemoteClient.streamExec buffered container stdout and stderr into unbounded bytes.Buffers via stdcopy.StdCopy and ReadFile streamed via unbounded cat, allowing runaway container output or large/device files (e.g. /dev/zero) to exhaust host RAM (OOM).

replaceTrafficTokenIfMatchScript patched traffic_access_token in raw JSON using non-escape-aware Lua pattern matching (".-"), corrupting stored session binding JSON in Redis when the existing token contained escaped quotes/backslashes or when another string field contained a lookalike substring.

SessionBoundManager.OpenSessionTerminal did not validate non-empty opts.Cwd through workspace.CleanWorkDirIn / cleanSessionWorkDir before admitUser and prepareSessionDirs (mkdir -p), permitting relative or uncleaned working directories.

invariants_checked: Redis ZSET lease admission atomically rejects new holds when the closed barrier key exists, prunes expired members via Redis server TIME, and never shortens ZSET PTTL below longer-lived active leases.
Local deadline timers subtract renewMargin (ttl/6) from request send time so unconfirmed leases and barriers fail closed (ErrLeaseLost) before server-side expiry.
RedisRegistry.Close defaults non-positive TTLs to DefaultHoldTTL consistently with Hold and MemoryRegistry.Close.
Barrier.Seal atomically verifies caller lock-token ownership in Lua before PERSIST, preventing a stale/expired barrier from stripping a replacement barrier's TTL or silently succeeding after expiry.
Zero weknora/wk_ residues; key prefix conventions align with genyee:sandbox:*.

findings.summary: RedisRegistry.Close failed when passed ttl <= 0 instead of defaulting to DefaultHoldTTL (unlike Hold and MemoryRegistry.Close), and Barrier.Seal executed bare PERSIST without verifying the barrier's lock token, allowing an expired barrier to strip a replacement barrier's TTL or fail to report ErrLeaseLost when its key had already expired.

findings.summary: Background execution paths (AutomationRunner.ownerContext, AgentCollaborationService.workerContext, and DataSourceService.ProcessSync) did not check tenant status ('inactive'/'disabled'/'suspended'), allowing scheduled automations, sub-agent delegations, and connector syncs to keep running for suspended workspaces; DataSourceService methods also lacked service-layer API-key scope and zero-tenant guards and did not verify syncLog.DataSourceID == payload.DataSourceID.

CustomAgent uses composite primary key (id, tenant_id), so ListSharesByAgent and ShareAgent's ErrAgentShareAlreadyExists recovery could match or leak shares belonging to another workspace with the same agent ID (and sharedAgentInfo/GetSharedAgentForTenant dereferenced share.Agent without nil guards); ShareKnowledgeBase's ErrKBShareAlreadyExists update path skipped SourceTenantID and canManageShare checks before overwriting permission.

DeleteKnowledgeBase and SetEmbeddingModel lacked service-layer AuthorizeTenantAPIKeyKnowledgeBases and owner-workspace enforcement (allowing narrowed API keys or org-shared Editors to mutate/delete owner KBs); CopyKnowledgeBase constructed newly cloned target KBs with only 5 fields, dropping Wiki-only IndexingStrategy, WikiConfig, ExtractConfig, QuestionGenerationConfig, and VectorStoreID; ProcessKBDelete bypassed storageResolver/resourceCatalog when deleting custom-backend files and images and called GetEmbeddingModel on empty Wiki-only EmbeddingModelID.

Shared-KB operations read ctx TenantInfo (the caller's workspace) instead of resolving the KB owner workspace's Tenant when selecting storage backends; CloneChunk and cloneFAQKnowledgeBase read source images through destination storage services (breaking cross-backend clones); Save/GetKBCloneProgress and Save/GetKnowledgeMoveProgress panicked on nil Redis in Lite mode and lacked tenant/API-key progress authorization; cleanupKnowledgeResources panicked when TenantInfoContextKey was absent and mutated shared Tenant.StorageUsed in place; user metadata inputs could overwrite reserved _knowledge_transfer and process_overrides keys.

ListFAQEntries, UpdateFAQEntry, and SearchFAQEntries did not call validateFAQTagScope (allowing same-tenant cross-KB tag binding/filtering), GetFAQEntry/SearchFAQEntries/ExportFAQEntries/ExportFAQEntriesJSON lacked service-layer KB read-grant and API-key scope checks, SearchFAQEntries panicked on nil request and dropped OnlyRecommended in the non-priority branch, UpsertFAQEntries accepted foreign-tenant caller TaskIDs and leaked uploaded EntriesURL blobs when Enqueue failed, GetFAQImportProgress lacked tenant/API-key checks and panicked without TenantIDContextKey, Lite-mode FAQ progress mutated shared pointers under -race, and duplicate ProcessFAQImport delivery overwrote Completed status.

EvaluationService.Evaluation and EvaluationResult used MustTenantIDFromContext (panicking on missing tenant), did not enforce AuthorizeTenantAPIKeyKnowledgeBases or KB ownership/grant checks on target KnowledgeBaseID, left EmbeddingModelID/SummaryModelID empty when ListModels was consulted, and retained terminal tasks in evaluationMemoryStorage without an upper bound.

RevertDocumentChunk queried GetChunkRevision before verifying writableChunk (exposing revision existence to unauthorized/viewer callers), DeleteGeneratedQuestion panicked via MustTenantIDFromContext on grant-only shared-Editor contexts and attempted vector index deletion on non-embedding Wiki-only KBs, and syncChunkIndex did not bind chunk.TenantID as execution tenant before retriever operations.

DataTableSummaryService.cleanupOnFailure used potentially cancelled ctx and stamped ParseStatusFailed even when Asynq retries remained; ImageMultimodalService read stored/local images without size caps and swallowed BatchIndex/model/engine errors leaving unindexed SQL chunks behind; enqueueSummaryRefresh overwrote completed SummaryStatus to failed on pre-enqueue config checks and RequestKnowledgeSummaryRefresh skipped loadKnowledgeWrite; spanTracker leaked starts map entries on SkipSpan/FinalizeAttempt/AbortAttempt; ArtifactCollector.hashStoredArtifact read stored blobs without MaxFileBytes cap; DispatchEmbedWebhook allowed payload keys to spoof envelope fields ('type', 'channel_id', 'session_id', 'timestamp') and drained unbounded HTTP response bodies.

resolveKnowledgeBases returned session/agent/all-tenant KB IDs and req.TagScopes without enforcing AuthorizeTenantAPIKeyKnowledgeBases or AuthorizeTenantAPIKeyOptionalTagIDs, allowing a KB-restricted TenantAPIKey to search unauthorized KBs via pre-configured session/agent KBs or auto-select fallback and pass unauthorized tag scopes.

UpdateModel dereferenced existingModel before nil-checking GetModelByID(nil, nil), did not pin model.TenantID = tenantID or model.IsBuiltin = false on non-builtin updates, and downloadModelAsync mutated caller-visible model fields in a background goroutine without cloning or guarding a nil ollamaService.

UserEnvService exposed the internal __workspace_scripts_policy__ sentinel TenantSandboxConfig row in ListScopes and accepted user env secrets against its ID, while TenantSandboxConfigService allowed creating a sandbox config named __workspace_scripts_policy__ (colliding with workspace scripts policy storage) and leaked the sentinel row in Inventory.

UpdateMCPService failed to clear AuthConfig.ClientSecret when MCPUpdateDropSecrets was requested, omitted Headers and MCPUpdateDropSecrets from needsReconnect detection, lacked nil s.mcpManager guards on disconnect paths, and TestMCPService omitted caller tenant fallback and MCPOAuthPrincipal propagation for OAuth-backed MCP transports.

ClearSessionMessages queried GetKnowledgeIDsBySessionID after DeleteMessagesBySessionID had already deleted the session messages rows (leaving session-uploaded temporary knowledge orphaned on clear), launched cleanup even if message deletion failed, and rerankResults sliced results[rr.Index] without guarding negative provider indices.

GenerateTitleAsync passed the caller *types.Session pointer directly into a background goroutine that mutated session.Title concurrently with caller reads/serialization, UpdateSession did not check existing == nil when GetByID returned (nil, nil), and forkOnSharedMachine omitted Kind: source.Kind when persisting forked sessions.

homeOrFirstMembershipTenant checked raw user.CanAccessAllTenants instead of access.UserCanAccessAllTenants(user, s.config) (honoring stale DB flags when CrossTenantAccessEnabled was disabled), AdminResetPassword left Preferences.OidcOnlyLogin = true so newly reset local passwords could still not sign in, and exchangeOIDCCode/fetchOIDCUserInfo used unbounded io.ReadAll on external IdP responses.

matchesBlacklistRule checked strings.HasPrefix(rule, "/") && strings.HasSuffix(rule, "/") without requiring len(rule) >= 2, causing a single-character "/" blacklist rule to panic on rule[1:len(rule)-1] during web search result filtering.

Zip skill bundle extraction did not normalize Windows backslash path separators or reject Windows drive-prefixed paths, cast UncompressedSize64 directly to int64 before checking >= 1<<63 (allowing negative int64 wraparound), sliced UTF-8 file previews mid-rune, tied trySkillBundle singleflight builds to the first caller's cancellable context, and did not release SubscribeProgress concurrency slots automatically when subCtx cancelled.

WorkspaceCheckpointer interpolated messageID inside single quotes (commit -m 'turn:%s') without shellSingleQuote (allowing single-quote shell injection if messageID was unvalidated), and workspaceLayoutFor executed destructive git --work-tree clean/reset without requiring WorkspaceVersioning, non-host layout, non-"/" Root, and GitDir outside Root.

RunLint treated transient GetKnowledgeBatch repository errors as missing source documents (enabling AutoFix to soft-delete live wiki pages during DB hiccups) and marked any existing Knowledge ID live without checking kn.TenantID == tenantID and kn.KnowledgeBaseID == kbID.

CreatePage accepted caller-supplied ID, Version, InLinks, and DeletedAt fields on user-authored wiki pages, while withSlugLock released its Redis lock via unconditional DEL(lockKey) (risking deletion of a successor holder's lock after TTL expiry) and ProcessWikiFinalize renewed its lock via bare Expire instead of token-owned redislock.Renew.

wikiIngestService.isKnowledgeGone used unscoped GetKnowledgeByIDOnly without checking kn.TenantID or kn.KnowledgeBaseID, and mapOneDocument read kn.Title without tenant/KB verification. A document moved to another KB while wiki ingest was queued or mid-reduce (especially in Lite mode without Redis tombstones) or a foreign-tenant knowledge ID would be treated as live, leaking source titles/updates across KB or tenant boundaries.
